about.title: Placerville Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product can turn an ordinary afternoon in Placerville into a trip to the emergency room — a power tool that malfunctions in a garage off Placerville Drive, a faulty vehicle part that fails near Rt 50, or a household appliance that overheats without warning. California law generally lets injured people pursue these claims under strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product itself was unreasonably dangerous, not on proving someone was careless. That's a meaningful distinction for El Dorado County residents trying to sort out what happened and who might be responsible. We handle these claims directly on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand. If a defective product hurt you or someone in your household, holding onto the item and any packaging can matter later, and talking with our team early costs nothing.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Ease Your Burden
items.desc: Under California law, you often don't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused harm. We can help identify which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product. We can help sort out who was involved in getting that product to you.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Since these claims often hinge on the condition of the product itself, keeping it (and any packaging or instructions) can strengthen your claim. We can advise on how to safely preserve evidence.

items.question: What counts as a product defect under California law?
items.answer: There are generally three types: a design defect (the product is inherently unsafe even if made correctly), a manufacturing defect (something went wrong during production), or a warning defect (inadequate instructions or safety warnings). We can help figure out which category fits your situation.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California often applies strict liability to these cases, which means the focus is on the product's condition and whether it caused your injury, rather than on the manufacturer's state of mind. This can simplify part of what needs to be shown.

items.question: I was hurt by a product I bought locally in Placerville — does that change anything?
items.answer: Not automatically. Retailers, distributors, and manufacturers can all potentially share responsibility regardless of where the product was purchased, including local stores here in El Dorado County. We can look into the full supply chain to see who may be involved.

items.question: How do we work with you?
items.answer: We evaluate cases like this at no upfront cost. There's no obligation, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover money.
